def-aqft-profile-likelihood-ratio:
## Definition

Let $(S,\mathcal S)$ be a measurable data space, let $\nu$ be a measure on it, and let $\Psi$ and $H$ be nonempty parameter sets. For each $(\psi,\eta)\in\Psi\times H$, let $p_{\psi,\eta}:S\to[0,+\infty]$ be a specified measurable density with $\int_S p_{\psi,\eta}\,d\nu=1$. A specified pointwise version of each density is part of the model because an observed-data likelihood can depend on the representative chosen within an almost-everywhere equivalence class. The coordinate $\psi$ is the parameter of interest; $\eta$ is a nuisance coordinate, meaning that it is retained in the probability model but is not the parameter whose value is tested or reported. The common dominating measure $\nu$ and the full density family are part of the model.

For observed data $s\in S$, define the likelihood $L_s(\psi,\eta)=p_{\psi,\eta}(s)$. Take both suprema below in the extended real line and suppose the global supremum
$$M_s:=\sup_{(\psi',\eta')\in\Psi\times H}L_s(\psi',\eta')$$
satisfies $0<M_s<+\infty$. For each $\psi\in\Psi$, define the profile likelihood $M_s(\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in H}L_s(\psi,\eta)$ and the profile likelihood ratio
$$\lambda_s(\psi):=\frac{M_s(\psi)}{M_s}\in[0,1].$$
The associated likelihood-ratio statistic is
$$q_s(\psi):=\begin{cases}-2\log\lambda_s(\psi),&\lambda_s(\psi)>0,\\ +\infty,&\lambda_s(\psi)=0,\end{cases}$$
where $\log$ is the real natural logarithm on $(0,\infty)$. These definitions use suprema and do not require a maximizing parameter value to exist. The distribution of $q_s$, a p-value calibration, and the coverage of a confidence set require additional model and sampling assumptions; none follows from this definition.
def-aqft-calibrated-pvalue:
## Definition

Let $(S,\mathcal S,\{\mathbb P_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta})$ be a statistical model, let $\Theta_0\subseteq\Theta$ be a nonempty null set, and let $T:S\to\mathbb R$ be a statistic whose upper-tail sets are measurable. Fix an explicit calibration probability measure $Q_0$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B(\mathbb R))$ for the statistic under the null procedure. For a simple null $\Theta_0=\{\theta_0\}$, the exact calibration is $Q_0=\mathbb P_{\theta_0}\circ T^{-1}$. For a composite null or an asymptotic analysis, $Q_0$ is supplied by the specified calibration procedure, whose nuisance-parameter treatment and approximation assumptions are part of the data.

For an observed datum $s\in S$, with the convention that larger $T$ values are more extreme, the upper-tail p-value is
$$p_0(s):=Q_0\bigl(\{t\in\mathbb R:t\ge T(s)\}\bigr).$$
It is a probability under the stated null calibration for a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed one. It is not a probability assigned to the null hypothesis conditional on the data; no probability distribution on $\Theta$ is supplied by this definition. The definition alone establishes neither type-I error control nor super-uniformity; any such validity claim requires a separate argument for the specified sampling model and calibration. A lower-tail or two-sided procedure must specify its own measurable extremeness set instead of using the displayed upper-tail convention.
def-aqft-cls-exclusion-ratio:
## Definition

Let $(S,\mathcal S)$ be a data space with two supplied probability laws $\mathbb P_b$ and $\mathbb P_{s+b}$ for the background-only and signal-plus-background hypotheses. Fix a statistic $T:S\to\mathbb R$ for which larger values are more incompatible with the signal-plus-background hypothesis and for which every upper-tail set is measurable. For observed datum $x\in S$, set $R_x:=\{y\in S:T(y)\ge T(x)\}$ and define
$$\mathrm{CL}_b(x):=\mathbb P_b(R_x),\qquad \mathrm{CL}_{s+b}(x):=\mathbb P_{s+b}(R_x).$$
When $\mathrm{CL}_b(x)>0$, the modified-frequentist exclusion ratio is
$$\mathrm{CL}_s(x):=\frac{\mathrm{CL}_{s+b}(x)}{\mathrm{CL}_b(x)}.$$
A reported exclusion rule at threshold $\alpha\in(0,1)$ excludes a specified signal-plus-background hypothesis when its supplied analysis has $\mathrm{CL}_s(x)<\alpha$. The likelihood ratio, test statistic, nuisance treatment, and sampling laws are part of the specified analysis. The ratio is not itself a probability or a frequentist coverage level; in the cited method it is a conservative, frequentist-motivated approximation used to present exclusion results. It does not give the probability that a signal model is true or false.

experimental_contract.Setup:
The ATLAS collaboration combines previously measured Higgs and simplified-template-cross-section observables, di-Higgs, diboson, vector-boson-fusion $Zjj$, high-mass Drell–Yan, top-quark distributions, and electroweak precision inputs. The proton-proton LHC inputs use 13 TeV Run 2 data and input-specific integrated luminosities spanning about $36$–$140\ {\rm fb}^{-1}$; the combined electroweak precision inputs also include LEP and SLD data. Integrated luminosity is the calibrated exposure assigned to a data sample, not a count of selected events. The input measurements retain their own observable definitions and selections.

The fit uses the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT): the Standard Model field content is supplemented by higher-dimension gauge-invariant operators. It fits 48 dimension-six Warsaw-basis coefficients or coefficient combinations. The reference normalization $\Lambda=1\ {\rm TeV}$ fixes how the reported coefficients are quoted; it is not a measured new-particle mass.
experimental_contract.Procedure: The collaboration constructs a joint likelihood from the input analyses, using Poisson terms for event-count inputs and Gaussian terms for measurement inputs where specified. It checks overlaps among event-based inputs using event identifiers, bootstrap studies, and selections; identified overlaps are removed or handled as stated in the article. Experimental and theoretical nuisance parameters encode systematic and theory uncertainties and are profiled subject to the source's constraints and correlation scheme. Profiling means maximizing the likelihood over nuisance parameters at each fixed coefficient value; the resulting profile-likelihood ratio compares that constrained maximum with the unrestricted maximum. The collaboration uses its stated one-dimensional likelihood-ratio calibration after checking the applicability of the asymptotic approximation. These are the reported analysis choices, not a reconstruction of the component likelihoods.
experimental_contract.Observations: The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the Standard Model and quotes a $99\%$ compatibility $p$-value for its specified goodness-of-fit test. It also identifies an electroweak-precision coefficient direction, denoted $c^{[19]}_{HVV,Vff}$ in the article, as pulled by the known tension between the measured $A_{\rm FB}^{b,c}$ asymmetries and the Standard Model prediction. The overall fit statement therefore does not mean that every coefficient is individually within two standard deviations. A $p$-value is a tail probability under the stated null calibration, not the probability that the Standard Model is true.
experimental_contract.Uncertainty: The reported likelihood carries statistical, detector, theory, and other systematic uncertainties with the correlations adopted for the input measurements. The article describes checks and special handling for shared-event inputs. This item does not recreate the raw-event record, rerun detector reconstruction, validate every input calibration, or independently estimate a covariance matrix. The reported $p$-value and intervals inherit those source-level assumptions.
experimental_contract.Interpretation: The result is a source-defined constraint on the selected 48 coefficient directions and data inputs. The reported parameterization retains linear and quadratic dimension-six contributions while omitting dimension-eight interference terms at order $\Lambda^{-4}$; its quadratic fit is therefore not a complete expansion to that order. The fit neither proves the SMEFT model nor establishes or excludes new physics in general. Its statistical conclusions remain conditional on the chosen observables, input likelihoods, nuisance model, coefficient truncation, and stated asymptotic calibration.

## Setup

The fit uses the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT): the Standard Model field content is supplemented by higher-dimension gauge-invariant operators. It fits 48 dimension-six Warsaw-basis coefficients or coefficient combinations. The reference normalization $\Lambda=1\ {\rm TeV}$ fixes how the reported coefficients are quoted; it is not a measured new-particle mass.

## Procedure

The collaboration constructs a joint likelihood from the input analyses, using Poisson terms for event-count inputs and Gaussian terms for measurement inputs where specified. It checks overlaps among event-based inputs using event identifiers, bootstrap studies, and selections; identified overlaps are removed or handled as stated in the article. These are the reported analysis choices, not a reconstruction of the component likelihoods.

## Observations

The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the Standard Model and quotes a $99\%$ compatibility $p$-value for its specified goodness-of-fit test. It also identifies an electroweak-precision coefficient direction, denoted $c^{[19]}_{HVV,Vff}$ in the article, as pulled by the known tension between the measured $A_{\rm FB}^{b,c}$ asymmetries and the Standard Model prediction. The overall fit statement therefore does not mean that every coefficient is individually within two standard deviations. A $p$-value is a tail probability under the stated null calibration, not the probability that the Standard Model is true.

The reported likelihood carries statistical, detector, theory, and other systematic uncertainties with the correlations adopted for the input measurements. The article describes checks and special handling for shared-event inputs. This item does not recreate the raw-event record, rerun detector reconstruction, validate every input calibration, or independently estimate a covariance matrix. The reported $p$-value and intervals inherit those source-level assumptions.

## Interpretation

The result is a source-defined constraint on the selected 48 coefficient directions and data inputs. The reported parameterization retains linear and quadratic dimension-six contributions while omitting dimension-eight interference terms at order $\Lambda^{-4}$; its quadratic fit is therefore not a complete expansion to that order. The fit neither proves the SMEFT model nor establishes or excludes new physics in general. Its statistical conclusions remain conditional on the chosen observables, input likelihoods, nuisance model, coefficient truncation, and stated asymptotic calibration.

experimental_contract.Setup:
CMS PAS SMP-25-002, dated 30 July 2026, reports a preliminary detector-level combination of ten electroweak multiboson measurements using CMS proton-proton data from 2016–2018 at $\sqrt{s}=13\ {\rm TeV}$ and reported integrated luminosity $138\ {\rm fb}^{-1}$. 

**Operational notation.** Use natural units $c=1$ and laboratory four-vector coordinates $P=(E,p_x,p_y,p_z)$, with the beam as the $z$ axis. The center-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}$ is the invariant energy of the incoming proton pair. Write $\mathbf p_T=(p_x,p_y)$ and $p_T=\sqrt{p_x^2+p_y^2}$. For a nonzero three-momentum with polar angle $0<\theta<\pi$ to the beam, pseudorapidity is $\eta=-\log\tan(\theta/2)$; azimuth $\phi$ is the direction of $\mathbf p_T$ modulo $2\pi$ when $p_T>0$. The separation $\Delta\phi$ is the smaller azimuthal angle in $[0,\pi]$, and, with $\Delta\eta=\eta_i-\eta_j$, $\Delta R_\eta=\sqrt{(\Delta\eta)^2+(\Delta\phi)^2}$. For a source-selected finite set of reconstructed four-vectors whose sum is nonzero future causal (total energy $E_\Sigma>0$ and $E_\Sigma^2\ge|\mathbf p_\Sigma|^2$, where $E_\Sigma=\sum E$ and $\mathbf p_\Sigma=\sum\mathbf p$), its invariant mass is $m=\sqrt{(\sum E)^2-|\sum\mathbf p|^2}$, with zero mass for a null sum, as in the supplied total-four-momentum definition. The labels $m_{jj}$ and $m_{\ell\ell}$ apply this definition to the selected jet or lepton pair. Candidate masses such as $m_{WV}$ use the source's chosen reconstructed candidates; no unreported neutrino-reconstruction prescription is supplied here. Integrated luminosity is the reported collision exposure in inverse-area units $\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$.

**Channel and reconstruction labels.** SM means Standard Model, SMEFT Standard Model effective field theory, EW electroweak, QCD quantum chromodynamics, MC Monte Carlo simulation, and LO leading perturbative order. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and the strong coupling $\alpha_s$ are the source-specified theory inputs for incoming-hadron constituents and strong-interaction strength in its factorization scheme; no unreported numerical functions are supplied. VBS means vector-boson scattering and VBF vector-boson fusion: here these name the source's EW two-boson or single-boson-plus-tagging-jet event categories, not a claimed gauge-invariant separation of an amplitude. $W$ and $Z$ are the charged and neutral weak bosons, $V$ denotes either, $\ell$ denotes an electron or muon unless a tau is stated, and $j$ denotes a reconstructed jet. The notation $jj$ denotes the source-selected pair of tagging jets, whose event-selection role is distinct from b tagging. A $\tau_h$ is a reconstructed candidate for the visible hadronic products of a tau decay, not a directly measured complete tau four-momentum. “Same/opposite sign” refers to reconstructed electric charge, and lepton “flavour” here distinguishes the named lepton species.

The missing transverse momentum vector $\mathbf p_T^{\mathrm{miss}}$ is the source's negative transverse-momentum sum over its chosen reconstructed particles, with its source-specified weighting and calibration corrections; $p_T^{\mathrm{miss}}=|\mathbf p_T^{\mathrm{miss}}|$. Appendix A identifies PUPPI, pileup-per-particle identification, as part of that reconstruction. Pileup means additional proton-proton interactions in the same or nearby bunch crossings. The exact PUPPI weights and correction map are source inputs not provided by this PAS and are not reconstructed here. Particle-flow reconstruction likewise names the source's map from tracker, calorimeter and muon information to identified particle candidates, not an independently reproduced detector-response model.

A b tag is the source's Boolean jet-selection decision intended to identify jets containing b-hadron decay products; its efficiency and misidentification are empirical calibration quantities, not proof of a jet's origin. DNN and BDT mean deep neural network and boosted decision tree. Operationally their scores are fixed source-supplied functions $s:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ of the source's reconstructed feature vectors. A working point is a specified cut on such a score. The DeepJet medium b-tag decision, DNN/BDT scores, features, trained weights and calibration maps remain source-labelled inputs; reported thresholds are retained without treating scores as probabilities or inventing the missing functions. A control region is a selected event subset used to constrain background predictions; a signal region is the selected subset used for the reported coefficient fit. “Nonprompt” leptons denote source-classified candidates not originating in the targeted prompt electroweak decay; charge misidentification denotes an incorrect reconstructed charge. Leading/subleading refers to decreasing $p_T$ within the selected collection.

Its ten inputs are VBS same-sign $WW$ with electrons/muons and with a hadronic $\tau$, opposite-sign $WW$, $WZ$, semileptonic $WV$ and $ZV$; VBF $Wjj$ and $Zjj$; opposite-sign diboson $WW$; and triboson $VVV$ without photons. The common fit varies the six CP-even bosonic Warsaw coefficients associated with $O_W,O_{HW},O_{HWB},O_{H\square},O_{HB},O_{HD}$. Only the source's specified bosonic SMEFT signal model is tested; other operators are not simultaneously constrained.

The apparatus includes the 3.8 T solenoid, silicon tracker, electromagnetic and hadron calorimeters, forward calorimeters and muon chambers. The report describes hardware and high-level triggering, full GEANT4 detector simulation and particle-flow reconstruction. Its statistical combination assumes nonoverlapping input phase spaces and conditional count independence in its likelihood model, while shared nuisance parameters encode correlated systematic effects. The PAS reports 163 signal/control regions, 912 bins and 3.39 million observed events, with 562 independent nuisance parameters. These are collaboration-reported combination totals, not independently recounted events.
experimental_contract.Procedure:
**Signal model and controls.** The report uses MADGRAPH5_aMC@NLO v2.6.5 and SMEFTSIM at leading order for SMEFT electroweak signals. Per-event weights at the SM point, individual coefficients $\pm1$ and coefficient-pair points reconstruct linear interference, squared dimension-six and mixed quadratic terms. CMS reports per-analysis closure checks against directly generated components. PYTHIA with the CP5 tune, NNPDF3.1 distributions, pileup matched to data and GEANT4 propagate predictions to detector level. Backgrounds are SM-only in this interpretation. Nonprompt leptons, electron charge misidentification and some vector-boson-plus-jets contributions use data control regions; irreducible backgrounds generally use simulation. The PAS gives analysis-dependent generator choices, rather than one universal background generator.

**Jet-clustering definition and source-specific variables.** For the referenced inclusive anti-$k_T$ algorithm, take a finite list of particle/pseudojet four-vectors (a pseudojet is a temporary merged object) with positive transverse momentum and finite rapidity $y=\tfrac12\log[(E+p_z)/(E-p_z)]$, where $E>|p_z|$. Use $\Delta R_{y,ij}^2=(y_i-y_j)^2+(\Delta\phi_{ij})^2$, not pseudorapidity separation for a massive pseudojet. With radius $R>0$, form $d_{ij}=\min(p_{T,i}^{-2},p_{T,j}^{-2})\Delta R_{y,ij}^2/R^2$ and $d_{iB}=p_{T,i}^{-2}$. Repeatedly select the smallest distance: for a pair, replace it by a recombined pseudojet; for a beam distance, declare that pseudojet a final inclusive jet and remove it. Recalculate distances and continue until the list is empty. In the E-scheme specified as FastJet's default, pair recombination is the four-vector sum $P_{ij}=P_i+P_j$. This prescription is understood on admissible inputs/intermediate pseudojets with a fixed implementation tie rule; zero-transverse-momentum, beam-collinear and exact-tie policies are not independently specified by the PAS. Cacciari–Salam–Soyez §1 supplies the anti-$k_T$ distances and clustering steps; the FastJet manual supplies the E-scheme merge. The PAS states $R=0.4$ but does not re-specify that software's complete recombination configuration or calibrations, so this defines the referenced standard procedure without claiming an audit of the CMS implementation.

For the dilepton Zeppenfeld variable, the actual displayed definition in PAS §7, printed p. 9, is $Z_\ell=\eta_\ell-\tfrac12(\eta_{j_1}+\eta_{j_2})$ and $Z_{\ell\ell}=\tfrac12|Z_{\ell_1}+Z_{\ell_2}|$. This was visually checked; no alternative normalization by jet separation is substituted. By contrast, $m_T^{WZ}$, $m_T^{WW}$ and $m_T^{W_2}$ remain the PAS-labelled transverse-mass discriminant/selection inputs; Appendix A associates the last with the subleading lepton. Their exact pointwise variants are not specified in the inspected PAS text and are not inferred from the labels. Formally they are fixed source-input functions of its reconstructed event variables with energy units; this account preserves their reported cuts without evaluating an invented formula.

**Selections and fitted observables.** Table 3 and Appendices A–C state the following combination-level inputs:

| Input | Reported selection/category and fitted observable |
|---|---|
| VBS opposite-sign $WW$ | Opposite-charge, opposite-flavour leptons with tagging jets; dijet mass, with the 2017–2018 sample split at dilepton Zeppenfeld variable 1 and a separate 2016 category |
| VBS same-sign $WW(e,\mu)$ and $WZ$ | Same-sign dileptons or three leptons with an opposite-sign same-flavour pair, plus VBS tagging jets; flattened $(m_{jj},m_{\ell\ell})$ or $(m_T^{WZ},m_{jj})$ bins; extra-lepton/b-jet vetoes suppress top and diboson backgrounds |
| VBS same-sign $WW(\tau_h)$ | Lepton/hadronic-$\tau$ final state; SMEFT DNN score in five bins with edges $0,0.264,0.405,0.517,0.608,1$ |
| VBF $W$ and $Z$ | One isolated lepton with missing transverse momentum or opposite-charge same-flavour dileptons, respectively, with separated tagging jets; $\Delta\phi_{jj}$, with DNN selection above 0.5 for $W$ and DNN-score windows for $Z$; $W$+jets/top control regions constrain backgrounds |
| VBS $WV$ and $ZV$ | Leptonic plus hadronic vector-boson decay topologies; $m_{WV}$ in DNN-score categories and $m_{ZV}$ in b-tag/b-veto categories |
| Triboson $VVV$ | Lepton/$\tau_h$/large-radius vector-jet multiplicities, with charge/flavour/$Z$-mass subdivisions; generally scalar transverse-momentum sums, with BDT/kinematic categories for hadronic-$\tau$ channels and additional channel-dependent mass discriminants |
| Diboson $WW$ | Opposite-charge $e\mu$, 0- and 1-jet categories; dilepton mass, with top-enriched control data and a data-driven nonprompt-lepton estimate |

Appendix A explicitly requires leading/subleading diboson leptons above 25/20 GeV, vetoes extra loose leptons above 10 GeV, and uses missing transverse momentum above 20 GeV, $p_T^{\ell\ell}>30$ GeV and $m_{\ell\ell}>20$ GeV. It describes anti-$k_T$ jets with radius 0.4, $p_T>30$ GeV and $|\eta|<4.7$, and a signal-region b-jet veto together with transverse-mass requirements $m_T^{WW}>60$ GeV and $m_T^{W_2}>30$ GeV. A top-enriched control region requires a b-tagged jet, $m_{\ell\ell}>50$ GeV and $m_T^{W_2}>30$ GeV. The report also describes tighter multivariate lepton identification in the VBS reinterpretations. Cuts and calibration constants not actually supplied by this PAS are not filled in from presumed standard CMS practice; Table 3 refers full original selection definitions to the input-analysis papers.

**Likelihood and test calibration.** For bin counts $n_k$, the reported model is a product of Poisson terms with means $\mu_k(\mathbf c,\theta)=N_k(\mathbf c,\theta)+b_k(\theta)$ and auxiliary-data constraint likelihoods $\pi_j(\widetilde\theta_j\mid\theta_j)$. The signal includes SM, linear, quadratic and pairwise mixed coefficient contributions; backgrounds are coefficient-independent. The count model is interpreted only where all Poisson means are finite and nonnegative; no unreported fit parameter range is reconstructed. The auxiliary constraints are not posterior probabilities for nuisance parameters. CMS uses COMBINE/RooFit/RooStats to profile nuisances in $q(\mathbf c)=-2\log[L(\mathbf c,\widehat{\widehat\theta})/L(\widehat{\mathbf c},\widehat\theta)]$. Individual fits fix the other five coefficients to zero; two-coefficient scans fix the other four; fully profiled scans float all other coefficients and nuisances.

Section 5 assumes Wilks' theorem and uses $q<1,4$ for one-dimensional 68.3%, 95.4% intervals, and $q<2.3,6.18$ for two-dimensional regions. The table/figure labels abbreviate these as 68%/95%. ## Setup

**Operational notation.** Use natural units $c=1$ and laboratory four-vector coordinates $P=(E,p_x,p_y,p_z)$, with the beam as the $z$ axis. The center-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}$ is the invariant energy of the incoming proton pair. Write $\mathbf p_T=(p_x,p_y)$ and $p_T=\sqrt{p_x^2+p_y^2}$. For a nonzero three-momentum with polar angle $0<\theta<\pi$ to the beam, pseudorapidity is $\eta=-\log\tan(\theta/2)$; azimuth $\phi$ is the direction of $\mathbf p_T$ modulo $2\pi$ when $p_T>0$. The separation $\Delta\phi$ is the smaller azimuthal angle in $[0,\pi]$, and, with $\Delta\eta=\eta_i-\eta_j$, $\Delta R_\eta=\sqrt{(\Delta\eta)^2+(\Delta\phi)^2}$. For a source-selected finite set of reconstructed four-vectors whose sum is nonzero future causal (total energy $E_\Sigma>0$ and $E_\Sigma^2\ge|\mathbf p_\Sigma|^2$, where $E_\Sigma=\sum E$ and $\mathbf p_\Sigma=\sum\mathbf p$), its invariant mass is $m=\sqrt{(\sum E)^2-|\sum\mathbf p|^2}$, with zero mass for a null sum, as in the supplied total-four-momentum definition. The labels $m_{jj}$ and $m_{\ell\ell}$ apply this definition to the selected jet or lepton pair. Candidate masses such as $m_{WV}$ use the source's chosen reconstructed candidates; no unreported neutrino-reconstruction prescription is supplied here. Integrated luminosity is the reported collision exposure in inverse-area units $\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$.

**Channel and reconstruction labels.** SM means Standard Model, SMEFT Standard Model effective field theory, EW electroweak, QCD quantum chromodynamics, MC Monte Carlo simulation, and LO leading perturbative order. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and the strong coupling $\alpha_s$ are the source-specified theory inputs for incoming-hadron constituents and strong-interaction strength in its factorization scheme; no unreported numerical functions are supplied. VBS means vector-boson scattering and VBF vector-boson fusion: here these name the source's EW two-boson or single-boson-plus-tagging-jet event categories, not a claimed gauge-invariant separation of an amplitude. $W$ and $Z$ are the charged and neutral weak bosons, $V$ denotes either, $\ell$ denotes an electron or muon unless a tau is stated, and $j$ denotes a reconstructed jet. The notation $jj$ denotes the source-selected pair of tagging jets, whose event-selection role is distinct from b tagging. A $\tau_h$ is a reconstructed candidate for the visible hadronic products of a tau decay, not a directly measured complete tau four-momentum. “Same/opposite sign” refers to reconstructed electric charge, and lepton “flavour” here distinguishes the named lepton species.

The missing transverse momentum vector $\mathbf p_T^{\mathrm{miss}}$ is the source's negative transverse-momentum sum over its chosen reconstructed particles, with its source-specified weighting and calibration corrections; $p_T^{\mathrm{miss}}=|\mathbf p_T^{\mathrm{miss}}|$. Appendix A identifies PUPPI, pileup-per-particle identification, as part of that reconstruction. Pileup means additional proton-proton interactions in the same or nearby bunch crossings. The exact PUPPI weights and correction map are source inputs not provided by this PAS and are not reconstructed here. A b tag is the source's Boolean jet-selection decision intended to identify jets containing b-hadron decay products; its efficiency and misidentification are empirical calibration quantities, not proof of a jet's origin. A control region is a selected event subset used to constrain background predictions; a signal region is the selected subset used for the reported coefficient fit. “Nonprompt” leptons denote source-classified candidates not originating in the targeted prompt electroweak decay; charge misidentification denotes an incorrect reconstructed charge. exp-aqft-atlas-tau-squark-gluino-search-.physical_scope: ATLAS search for R-parity-conserving simplified squark and gluino models in tau, jets, and missing-transverse-momentum final states. The reported contours and local compatibility value apply only to the source's stated spectra, branching fractions, and analysis.

empirical_result.observation: The paper reports no significant overall deviation, a local p-value of 0.00058 (3.2 standard deviations) at its GG(1300,1200) benchmark, and observed 95% CLs exclusion contours reaching up to 2.25 TeV for gluinos in the machine-learning analysis and 2.3 TeV in the cut-and-count analysis, with squark reaches of 1.35 TeV and 1.7 TeV respectively. These values are model- and strategy-specific.
empirical_result.uncertainty: The analysis profiles source-correlated experimental and background nuisance parameters in a binned likelihood, validates its asymptotic approximation against simulation, and reports integrated-luminosity uncertainties of 0.83% for 13 TeV data and 2.0% for 13.6 TeV data. Theory cross-section uncertainty is shown as a variation of contours rather than profiled as an experimental nuisance in the fit.
empirical_result.conditions: ATLAS 140 fb^-1 at 13 TeV (2015–2018) plus 51.8 fb^-1 at 13.6 TeV (2022–2023), three orthogonal hadronic-tau/lepton channels, and the collaboration's R-parity-conserving simplified spectra with its stated intermediate-mass, branching-fraction, and narrow-width assumptions.

experimental_contract.Setup:
ATLAS searches for pair-produced gluinos or first- and second-generation left-handed squarks in final states with hadronically decaying tau leptons, jets, and missing transverse momentum. The dataset combines $140\ {\rm fb}^{-1}$ of $13\ {\rm TeV}$ proton-proton data from 2015–2018 with $51.8\ {\rm fb}^{-1}$ at $13.6\ {\rm TeV}$ from 2022–2023. The three orthogonal channels require (1) exactly one hadronically decaying tau and no electron or muon, (2) exactly one hadronic tau and at least one electron or muon, or (3) at least two hadronic taus. Events are selected using missing-transverse-momentum triggers with thresholds between 70 and 115 GeV; their reported efficiencies are typically 80–90% and about 40% in the most compressed signal region.

The interpretation adopts $R$-parity-conserving simplified models, where $R=(-1)^{3(B-L)+2s}$ is a conserved $Z_2$ quantum number, $B$ and $L$ denote baryon and lepton number, $s$ denotes spin, Standard Model particles are even, and their superpartners are odd. The gluino may decay through a virtual squark; squark decays proceed through the lightest chargino or next-to-lightest neutralino. The tau-slepton and tau-sneutrino are co-next-to-lightest supersymmetric particles. The lightest neutralino is assumed bino-like, meaning predominantly the superpartner of the hypercharge gauge boson, and the lightest chargino and next-to-lightest neutralino are wino-like, meaning predominantly superpartners of weak gauge bosons. The source fixes
$$m(\tilde\chi_1^\pm)=m(\tilde\chi_2^0)=\frac{m(\tilde g\text{ or }\tilde q)+m(\tilde\chi_1^0)}{2},\qquad m(\tilde\tau)=m(\tilde\nu_\tau)=\frac{m(\tilde\chi_1^\pm)+m(\tilde\chi_1^0)}{2}.$$
The chargino and next-to-lightest-neutralino branching fractions to tau-slepton or tau-sneutrino modes are set to $50\%$, other supersymmetric couplings are set to zero, and the narrow-width approximation treats intermediate resonances as on-shell because their widths are assumed small relative to their masses. These choices define the reported simplified-model contours.
experimental_contract.Procedure:
The reported observables include missing transverse momentum, defined as the magnitude of the negative vector sum of reconstructed electrons, muons, hadronic taus, jets, and a track-based soft term, along with channel-specific kinematic variables. Jets are reconstructed with the anti-$k_t$ algorithm at radius $R=0.4$ and calibrated using simulation and in-situ measurements. Hadronic tau candidates are seeded by anti-$k_t$ jets, calibrated with a dedicated visible-tau energy-scale procedure, and selected with one or three tracks and a medium identification working point. Light leptons and jets have source-defined identification, overlap-removal, and kinematic selections. The analysis estimates jets misidentified as tau leptons with a data-driven fake-factor method and uses both cut-and-count and machine-learning strategies.

For each strategy the collaboration fits selected binned data with a likelihood containing Poisson event-count terms and constrained systematic and background nuisance parameters; source-stated correlations are retained. The statistic is a profile likelihood ratio, formed by maximizing over nuisance parameters at fixed signal-model parameters and comparing with the unrestricted fit. ATLAS uses the asymptotic approximation after validating it against simulated ensembles. It excludes a tested signal point when the source-defined $CL_s$ ratio falls below $0.05$; $CL_s$ is the signal-plus-background tail probability divided by the corresponding background tail probability under the same source-defined test ordering, not a posterior probability or exact coverage statement.
experimental_contract.Observations: The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the background-only expectation. Its most compatible machine-learning benchmark, labelled GG(1300,1200), has a local $p$-value $0.00058$, quoted as $3.2$ standard deviations; this is a local value at the tested benchmark, not an overall search significance. The observed $95\%$ $CL_s$ contours reach gluino masses up to $2.25\ {\rm TeV}$ in the machine-learning analysis and $2.3\ {\rm TeV}$ in the cut-and-count analysis, and squark masses up to $1.35\ {\rm TeV}$ and $1.7\ {\rm TeV}$, respectively, in the corresponding source-defined mass planes.
experimental_contract.Uncertainty: The fit includes the collaboration's statistical, detector, background, and theoretical nuisance constraints with source-reported correlations. The reported integrated-luminosity uncertainties are $0.83\%$ for the 13 TeV sample and $2.0\%$ for the 13.6 TeV sample. The theory cross-section uncertainty is displayed as a contour variation rather than profiled as an experimental nuisance. The observed contour uses an asymptotic approximation checked against simulated ensembles. This record does not reprocess collision events or independently reconstruct the likelihood, object calibrations, or nuisance covariance.
experimental_contract.Interpretation: The local excess, $CL_s$ exclusions, and mass reaches are conditional on the three selected channels, the two analysis strategies, and the particular $R$-parity-conserving simplified spectra, midpoint mass relations, branching fractions, and narrow-width assumptions stated above. They do not rule out supersymmetry as a framework, establish a supersymmetry-breaking vacuum, or constrain spectra and decay patterns outside those parameterizations.

## Setup

ATLAS searches for pair-produced gluinos or first- and second-generation left-handed squarks in final states with hadronically decaying tau leptons, jets, and missing transverse momentum. The dataset combines $140\ {\rm fb}^{-1}$ of $13\ {\rm TeV}$ proton-proton data from 2015–2018 with $51.8\ {\rm fb}^{-1}$ at $13.6\ {\rm TeV}$ from 2022–2023. The three orthogonal channels require (1) exactly one hadronically decaying tau and no electron or muon, (2) exactly one hadronic tau and at least one electron or muon, or (3) at least two hadronic taus. Events are selected using missing-transverse-momentum triggers with thresholds between 70 and 115 GeV; their reported efficiencies are typically 80–90% and about 40% in the most compressed signal region.

The interpretation adopts $R$-parity-conserving simplified models, where $R=(-1)^{3(B-L)+2s}$ is a conserved $Z_2$ quantum number, $B$ and $L$ denote baryon and lepton number, $s$ denotes spin, Standard Model particles are even, and their superpartners are odd. The gluino may decay through a virtual squark; squark decays proceed through the lightest chargino or next-to-lightest neutralino. The tau-slepton and tau-sneutrino are co-next-to-lightest supersymmetric particles. The lightest neutralino is assumed bino-like, meaning predominantly the superpartner of the hypercharge gauge boson, and the lightest chargino and next-to-lightest neutralino are wino-like, meaning predominantly superpartners of weak gauge bosons. The source fixes
$$m(\tilde\chi_1^\pm)=m(\tilde\chi_2^0)=\frac{m(\tilde g\text{ or }\tilde q)+m(\tilde\chi_1^0)}{2},\qquad m(\tilde\tau)=m(\tilde\nu_\tau)=\frac{m(\tilde\chi_1^\pm)+m(\tilde\chi_1^0)}{2}.$$
The chargino and next-to-lightest-neutralino branching fractions to tau-slepton or tau-sneutrino modes are set to $50\%$, other supersymmetric couplings are set to zero, and the narrow-width approximation treats intermediate resonances as on-shell because their widths are assumed small relative to their masses. These choices define the reported simplified-model contours.

## Procedure

The reported observables include missing transverse momentum, defined as the magnitude of the negative vector sum of reconstructed electrons, muons, hadronic taus, jets, and a track-based soft term, along with channel-specific kinematic variables. Jets are reconstructed with the anti-$k_t$ algorithm at radius $R=0.4$ and calibrated using simulation and in-situ measurements. Hadronic tau candidates are seeded by anti-$k_t$ jets, calibrated with a dedicated visible-tau energy-scale procedure, and selected with one or three tracks and a medium identification working point. Light leptons and jets have source-defined identification, overlap-removal, and kinematic selections. The analysis estimates jets misidentified as tau leptons with a data-driven fake-factor method and uses both cut-and-count and machine-learning strategies.

For each strategy the collaboration fits selected binned data with a likelihood containing Poisson event-count terms and constrained systematic and background nuisance parameters; source-stated correlations are retained. The statistic is a profile likelihood ratio, formed by maximizing over nuisance parameters at fixed signal-model parameters and comparing with the unrestricted fit. ATLAS uses the asymptotic approximation after validating it against simulated ensembles. It excludes a tested signal point when the source-defined $CL_s$ ratio falls below $0.05$; $CL_s$ is the signal-plus-background tail probability divided by the corresponding background tail probability under the same source-defined test ordering, not a posterior probability or exact coverage statement.

## Observations

The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the background-only expectation. Its most compatible machine-learning benchmark, labelled GG(1300,1200), has a local $p$-value $0.00058$, quoted as $3.2$ standard deviations; this is a local value at the tested benchmark, not an overall search significance. The observed $95\%$ $CL_s$ contours reach gluino masses up to $2.25\ {\rm TeV}$ in the machine-learning analysis and $2.3\ {\rm TeV}$ in the cut-and-count analysis, and squark masses up to $1.35\ {\rm TeV}$ and $1.7\ {\rm TeV}$, respectively, in the corresponding source-defined mass planes.

## Uncertainty

The fit includes the collaboration's statistical, detector, background, and theoretical nuisance constraints with source-reported correlations. The reported integrated-luminosity uncertainties are $0.83\%$ for the 13 TeV sample and $2.0\%$ for the 13.6 TeV sample. The theory cross-section uncertainty is displayed as a contour variation rather than profiled as an experimental nuisance. The observed contour uses an asymptotic approximation checked against simulated ensembles. This record does not reprocess collision events or independently reconstruct the likelihood, object calibrations, or nuisance covariance.

## Interpretation

The local excess, $CL_s$ exclusions, and mass reaches are conditional on the three selected channels, the two analysis strategies, and the particular $R$-parity-conserving simplified spectra, midpoint mass relations, branching fractions, and narrow-width assumptions stated above. They do not rule out supersymmetry as a framework, establish a supersymmetry-breaking vacuum, or constrain spectra and decay patterns outside those parameterizations.
